entities.description: E-commerce orders from the web shop (Cosmos DB), one row per order version. The source re-emits an order when line items are added, so the same order_number can appear more than once in an extract; the latest document (by Cosmos _id) wins and earlier states are kept as history (SCD2). Nested line items, promotions and click-stream are parsed into typed arrays.

derived.order_gross_amount: CAST(aggregate(ordered_products, CAST(0 AS DOUBLE), (acc, p) -> acc + CAST(p.price AS DOUBLE) * CAST(p.qty AS DOUBLE)) AS DECIMAL(14,2))

column_comments.order_number: Business key of the order (web shop order number).
column_comments.source_document_id: Cosmos DB document _id; increases with insertion time and orders versions of the same order.
column_comments.customer_name: Customer name as captured at order time (may differ from the CRM master).
column_comments.number_of_line_items: Line-item count reported by the source (can lag ordered_products; see line_item_count).
column_comments.line_item_count: Actual number of entries in ordered_products.
column_comments.order_ts: Order timestamp (UTC), derived from the source epoch seconds. NULL for a small share of orders.
column_comments.ordered_products: Line items: product id, name, unit price, quantity, unit and optional promotion (discount rate applies to the line).
column_comments.clicked_items: Click-stream pairs [product_id, click_count] captured before checkout.
column_comments.promo_info: Promotions applied at order level (mirrors the line-level promotion_info).
column_comments.has_promotion: TRUE when at least one promotion was applied.
column_comments.order_gross_amount: Sum of price x quantity over ordered_products, before discounts.

quality_rules.name: order_ts_present
quality_rules.description: About 1% of source orders have no timestamp; they are kept but excluded from date joins.

quality_rules.name: line_items_parsed
quality_rules.description: ordered_products must parse into at least one line.

entities.description: Point-of-sale transactions exported to S3, one row per product sold (SCD1). The feed has no transaction identifier, so sale_id is a deterministic hash of the business columns; exact duplicate rows in the export collapse into one. The nested product JSON is parsed with regular expressions because ~8% of names contain unescaped quotes.

derived.sale_id: sha2(concat_ws('|', CAST(customer_id AS STRING), CAST(order_date AS STRING), product_json, listed_product_name, CAST(total_amount AS STRING)), 256)

column_comments.sale_id: Deterministic SHA-256 over customer, date, product payload and amount; stable across reloads.
column_comments.customer_name: Customer name as printed on the receipt.
column_comments.listed_product_name: Product name column from the export; often differs from the product actually sold (see product_name).
column_comments.product_id: Catalogue product id of the item sold (parsed from the product payload).
column_comments.product_name: Name of the item sold (parsed from the product payload; authoritative).
column_comments.currency: ISO currency code of the amounts.
column_comments.total_amount: Line total from the export (= unit_price x quantity).

quality_rules.name: product_parsed
quality_rules.expression: product_id IS NOT NULL AND product_id <> '' AND unit_price IS NOT NULL AND quantity IS NOT NULL

entities.description: Customer master from the CRM (Azure SQL). The source carries its own validity window (valid_from / valid_to) and can contain more than one version per customer; the latest source version per customer_id is loaded and change history across loads is kept (SCD2). Use is_current = true for the latest version and is_active for customers still open in the CRM.

derived.customer_type: CASE WHEN customer_name LIKE '%,%' THEN 'individual' ELSE 'organisation' END
derived.last_name: CASE WHEN customer_name LIKE '%,%' THEN trim(split_part(customer_name, ',', 1)) END
derived.first_name: CASE WHEN customer_name LIKE '%,%' THEN trim(split_part(customer_name, ',', 2)) END
derived.loyalty_segment_name: CASE loyalty_segment WHEN 0 THEN 'Bronze' WHEN 1 THEN 'Silver' WHEN 2 THEN 'Gold' WHEN 3 THEN 'Platinum' ELSE 'Unknown' END

column_comments.customer_name: Name as 'LAST, FIRST' for individuals or the organisation name.
column_comments.last_name: Family name for individuals; NULL for organisations.
column_comments.first_name: Given name(s) for individuals; NULL for organisations.
column_comments.state: US state code of the address.
column_comments.city: City of the address (may be missing).
column_comments.postcode: Postal code, normalised (no trailing .0; 0 becomes NULL).
column_comments.region: Region as captured by the CRM (inconsistent: state code or name).
column_comments.district: County / district as captured by the CRM (inconsistent codes and names).
column_comments.ship_to_address: Concatenated shipping address string from the CRM.
column_comments.source_valid_to: CRM validity end (epoch seconds); NULL while active.
column_comments.source_valid_to_ts: CRM validity end (UTC timestamp); NULL while active.
column_comments.is_active: TRUE when the CRM record is still open (no valid_to).
column_comments.units_purchased: Lifetime units purchased according to the CRM.
column_comments.loyalty_segment: Loyalty segment code 0-3 from the CRM.
column_comments.loyalty_segment_name: Loyalty segment label (0 Bronze, 1 Silver, 2 Gold, 3 Platinum).

quality_rules.name: unique_customer_id
quality_rules.description: Guaranteed after de-duplication on the latest source version.

quality_rules.name: coordinates_in_range
quality_rules.expression: lon BETWEEN -180 AND 180 AND lat BETWEEN -90 AND 90
